turns.assessment: The outage is a node-wide optical isolation pattern centred on S16: many unrelated services that all depend on roadm.S16 failed simultaneously, while services not depending on S16 remained operational. Bidirectional LOS/OSC alarms on multiple S16-facing degrees make individual client, transponder, amplifier, or single-span faults implausible. The best documented single cause is failure of the shared WSS port at roadm.S16.

proposals.rationale: All affected working paths share roadm.S16, and the simultaneous all-channel optical losses on multiple paths are consistent with channels being blocked at that common ROADM. Unaffected S22 services that avoid S16 strongly localize the cause there.
Recent maintenance at S16 and hard signal loss make a disconnected patch plausible, but one OMS input patch does not explain the simultaneous losses on several S16 degrees.

OSC and signal loss are compatible with a cut, but the alarms involve multiple distinct S16 links; explaining the complete pattern would require coincident cuts or a shared-duct event rather than one span fault.

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the event to roadm.S16 but does not identify one failed WSS input degree. Both the S03–S16 and S07–S16 directions show simultaneous loss indications, while the S22–S16 degree has unchanged monitoring; this does not uniquely select any one of the three candidate ports.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (3 locations); reported as a set

score.why: truth not in the reported set
